articles.title: The last klavern
articles.summary:
• The remnants of a Ku Klux Klan hall serve as a haunting reminder of America's racial history and the complexities of memory.  
• Preservation of such sites raises profound questions about how societies confront their dark legacies.  
• Engaging with the past can illuminate contemporary issues of racism and identity, fostering dialogue and understanding.  
• The intersection of architecture and history reveals the physical manifestations of ideologies that shape communities.  
• Ultimately, grappling with these spaces challenges us to redefine our narratives and confront uncomfortable truths.

articles.title: The horse made the state
articles.summary:
• The development of civilization was fundamentally driven by transportation, not agriculture.  
• Horses facilitated the movement of people and ideas, reshaping social structures and power dynamics.  
• Conquest, enabled by superior mobility, became a catalyst for state formation and territorial expansion.  
• The relationship between humans and horses illustrates the profound impact of animals on societal evolution.  
• Understanding history through the lens of transportation reveals the interconnectedness of culture, power, and technology.
